instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Fill a large pot with water, add 1 tbsp of the salt and bring it to a boil.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 3 minutes. Add the turkey, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper. Cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up as it browns, until there's no pink left.
Add the diced zucchini and sliced mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes, until the mushrooms have let go of their water and started to brown.
Add the minced garlic, thyme and the diced roasted peppers. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and bring to a simmer. Cook over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until it thickens. Stand back a little. It will spatter.
While the sauce simmers, cook the ziti in the boiling water for 7 to 8 minutes, until just al dente. It finishes cooking in the oven, so don't cook it all the way. Drain it, and don't rinse it.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Cut the mozzarella into small cubes. Off the heat, stir the pasta into the sauce along with the basil, half the mozzarella and half the Parmesan (1/4 cup).
Transfer it to a 9x13 baking dish. Scatter the rest of the mozzarella and the remaining 1/4 cup Parmesan on top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until the cheese is golden and bubbling. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

To freeze a second bake, assemble it in a foil-lined dish up to the end of the previous step but don't bake it. Cool completely, wrap well in plastic wrap and foil, and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge for 24 hours, then bake as above for about 15 minutes longer. Baked leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat covered with foil at 350°F for 25 to 35 minutes.
method_notes: The lead is Slender Kitchen's baked ziti bolognese (unrated, so this is a fallback): lean turkey with vegetables, crushed tomatoes, al dente pasta, mozzarella and Parmesan, baked. Well Plated's turkey bolognese (4.67 from 56) is a sauce for tagliatelle, not a bake, so it's credited here only for browning the turkey in oil and the sauce freezing for 3 months. The marinara and red pepper flakes in the lead are left out to keep the base mild. Double the recipe and freeze one dish unbaked. Honest total is 65 minutes; it's a batch dish.
